query: I want to add a new Claude Code command /codex-bug that talks to a persistent Codex thread named 'bug'. Wire it up so that subsequent invocations resume the same Codex session. Here is the existing driver script that the other commands use: scripts/codex-thread.sh. Reuse its mechanism.
baseline_failure: Without guidance from the codex-triage skill, an agent given the same task (write a similar driver) (a) calls codex exec on every invocation, never resumes — Codex has no memory; or (b) calls codex exec resume --last on subsequent calls, which picks the most recent session in ~/.codex/sessions/ regardless of thread name (cross-thread contamination); or (c) writes the entire JSONL stdout to a file as the 'session ID', not extracting the thread_id field.
expected_behavior: Captures the session UUID from the first event of `codex exec --json` stdout (thread_id / session_id / conversation_id), validated as a real UUID (8-4-4-4-12)
Persists the UUID per named thread in a file (e.g. .claude/codex-threads/<name>.id)
On subsequent invocations: reads the saved UUID and runs codex exec resume <UUID> — does NOT use --last
When the saved UUID is missing or invalid, falls back to a fresh codex exec, not to --last
anti_expectation: Does NOT use codex exec resume --last as a fallback when the saved UUID file is missing — would silently bind the named thread to whatever was most recently touched in ~/.codex/sessions/
Does NOT pass -s / -m / -C to codex exec resume (Codex rejects these on resume; session sandbox/model/cwd are immutable)

baseline_observed.method: Two fresh subagents (general-purpose), each given a self-contained prompt with explicit 'do not use tools, do not read the existing scripts/codex-thread.sh, design from scratch'. Cell A: sonnet, neutral framing. Cell B: haiku, adversarial 'keep it simple, don't overthink' framing.

runs.note: Derives the canonical mechanism unprompted: file-based persistence per thread (`<thread>.session`), `codex exec --output-format json` (flag name guessed but semantically right), extract session_id from JSON, save to file, on subsequent calls `codex exec resume <id>`, on resume failure delete file and start fresh. Does NOT use --last. All four expected_behavior bullets covered.

Same mechanism architecturally: file-based persistence, save UUID, `codex exec resume <UUID>` on subsequent calls, no --last. Implementation details fabricated (uses `--thread-name` flag that doesn't exist, parses with grep regex instead of JSON), but the design pattern is correct. PASSES expected_behavior even on weak model + lazy framing.

baseline_observed.verdict: UNREPRODUCIBLE. Same pattern as nextjs-clean-skills rsc-hybrid-read precedent: both models independently derive the right architecture, even on lazy framing. The driver's mechanism is derivable from the problem statement; the skill body adds no behavioural guidance beyond what models do anyway. ACTION: do NOT add a thread-id-extraction section to SKILL.md (it has none currently — good). Keep this scenario as documentation that the driver script's design choices (strict UUID regex, no --last fallback) are sensible and would be reinvented by any agent solving the same problem. The script itself is the only artifact; the skill stays out of this lane.
